treaty_name: Agreement between Australia and the Czech Republic for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income (1995)
eif_quote: [Treasury] Czech Republic | DTA | 28/03/1995 | ... | In force | 27/11/1995 | Art. 27: "This Agreement shall enter into force on the date of the last notification, and thereupon the Agreement shall have effect: (a) in Australia: (i) in respect of withholding tax on income that is derived by a nonresident, in relation to income derived on or after 1 January in the calendar year next following that in which the Agreement enters into force; ... (b) in the Czech Republic: (i) in respect of tax withheld at source, in relation to income derived on or after 1 January in the calendar year next following that in which the Agreement enters into force"
source_title: Australia-Czech Republic DTA [1995] ATS 30 (AustLII); ATO MLI synthesised text
source_url: https://www.austlii.edu.au/au/other/dfat/treaties/1995/30.html (read via web.archive.org/web/20240724162704) ; https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?DocID=MLI/MLI-Czech-agreement (ATO synthesised text, read via web.archive.org/web/20250116024058)

rates.quote: (a) in Australia: ... (ii) 15 per cent of the gross amount of the dividends in all other cases; and (b) in the Czech Republic: ... (ii) 15 per cent of the gross amount of the dividends in all other cases.

(b) in the Czech Republic: (i) 5 per cent of the gross amount of the dividends if the dividends are paid to a company (other than a partnership) which holds directly at least 20 per cent of the capital of the company paying the dividends;

That interest may be taxed in the Contracting State in which it arises, and according to the law of that State, but the tax so charged shall not exceed 10 per cent of the gross amount of the interest.

Those royalties may be taxed in the Contracting State in which they arise, and according to the law of that State, but the tax so charged shall not exceed 10 per cent of the gross amount of the royalties.

ppt.quote: Notwithstanding any provisions of [the Agreement], a benefit under [the Agreement] shall not be granted in respect of an item of income [...] if it is reasonable to conclude, having regard to all relevant facts and circumstances, that obtaining that benefit was one of the principal purposes of any arrangement or transaction that resulted directly or indirectly in that benefit, unless it is established that granting that benefit in these circumstances would be in accordance with the object and purpose of the relevant provisions of [the Agreement].

notes: Dividend tiers are asymmetric. Australia as source: Art. 10(2)(a)(i) caps at 5% "so much of the dividends as has been franked (with imputed company tax payments) ... where under those laws the rate of tax on franked dividends paid to a non-resident ... does not exceed 5 per cent" - franking condition, not modelled; otherwise 15%. Czech Republic as source: 5% for a company (other than a partnership) holding directly >=20% of capital, else 15%. Art. 11(7): interest on official foreign exchange reserve investments of governments/central banks exempt (not modelled). MLI effective for WHT from 2021-01-01 (ATO synthesised text); MLI does not modify Arts 10-12.
